stop_condition: Every claim in the D5-piece-2 brief is verified against the shipped code -- readers chained not reparsed, per-unit unit_hash never the whole-artifact design_hash, the new SPEC-INJECTED v1 grammar plus its reader, unbound-silent vs bound-unreadable-loud, and gates nothing -- and no finding at or above high remains in the gate, hook, or record-grammar paths.

findings.evidence: subagent-start.sh builds "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/specs/${design_task}.md" by raw interpolation at 4 live sites (:591 is header comment). Every other consumer, including cmd_design_unit_bind at qa-gate.sh:12104, resolves via design_artifact_path_for, which sanitises with tr -c A-Za-z0-9._- _ . The binding class at cmd_design_unit_show:53 is ^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$ and admits +; the sanitiser does not. Measured: design_task=a+b -> writer docs/specs/a+b.md, reader docs/specs/a_b.md; and + survives the SPEC-INJECTED capture class, so it round-trips into the reader.
findings.description: Two disagreeing artifact-path resolvers for one convention. For a design_task containing +, the hook injects from one file while spec-injection-status checks another: best case a permanent exit 2 (spec_injection_content_unreadable), worst case a false FRESH/STALE against an unrelated artifact; the three prompt-text sites would additionally direct the implementer at a filename that does not exist. NOT reachable from a bd-generated id (0 of 442 ids in the ledger snapshot contain +; BD_ID_RE excludes it) and --design-task is the only injection point, which is why this is medium and not high. The defect-family point: the author verified the upstream class prevents TRAVERSAL (correct -- I confirmed cmd_design_unit_show:53 refuses anything outside the class before bound:true, and a literal .. yields the harmless docs/specs/...md) and then relied on that for EQUIVALENCE, which does not follow. Fix is confined to this one file but is 4 sites, not 1.

findings.evidence: Reachability measured, not assumed: review-check.sh design-unit-json <valid-artifact> U9 returns rc 1 with error_key=unit_not_in_design, and qa-gate.sh design_unit_json explicitly maps that to printf ; return 0, so design_unit_content_hash returns rc 0 with empty stdout and cmd_spec_injection_status reaches if [ -z "$live_hash" ]. Neither design-accessors.test.sh Section 12 nor the component spec references it (grep for "no longer declared" / "amended away": no hits).
findings.description: The unit-amended-away-entirely STALE arm is live, reachable code with no assertion. It is one of the three fresh:false reasons the usage text advertises and the only one untested -- content-changed is 12.3, rebound is 12.4. Visibility-only impact in this slice since nothing gates on the reader.

findings.evidence: Seven error keys are defined in the new region; exactly one (spec_injection_source_unreadable) is asserted in Section 12. Unasserted: spec_injection_content_unreadable, design_binding_unreadable, spec_injection_record_malformed, envelope_construction_failed, jq_unavailable, missing_task_id, unknown_flag.
findings.description: Coverage question, not a defect. design_binding_unreadable is explicitly and honestly disclosed as non-discriminable in the function header (both readers share design_comments_json, so a store outage fails at the first call) -- that disclosure is good practice and is not counted against the author. spec_injection_record_malformed is correctly-scoped defence against a jq TOOL failure mid-run (both sites guard on rshape_rc -ne 0 and on post-extraction empty fields), not dead code and not a content coverage hole. The remaining six are a genuine gap worth one follow-up.

findings.evidence: unit_pretty is rendered verbatim into CONTEXT inside <subagent_assignment>. Transport is safe -- the envelope is built with jq -Rs . at :943 -- but the rendered prompt text is not tag-escaped.
findings.description: A design artifact whose text contained a literal </subagent_assignment> would render as a closing tag in the implementer prompt, letting artifact content impersonate the harness frame. The artifact is validate-design-gated, hash-bound and already a trusted instruction channel (instructing the implementer is the feature), so this is containment hygiene rather than a vulnerability.
